scope: Make the 100 active-playlist-per-channel cap safe under concurrent creates and deletes without serializing other channels.
implementation: PlaylistRepository exposes a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock keyed by channel id.
createPlaylist acquires the channel lock before COUNT and holds it through INSERT and audit in the same transaction.
deletePlaylist acquires the same channel lock before its scoped lookup and soft delete, so freeing a slot serializes with creates.

checks.name: postgres-concurrent-count-protocol
checks.command: DATABASE_URL=<fresh-disposable-PostgreSQL-17> DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED=<same> npx prisma migrate deploy && npx vitest run --config vitest.postgres.config.ts tests/postgres/playlist-limit-concurrency.pg.test.ts
covers: at 99 active playlists, two simultaneous creates yield one success, one PLAYLIST_LIMIT refusal and a final count of 100
successful creation writes exactly one audit row
soft delete frees a slot for a replacement playlist
a foreign-channel playlist id is refused without deletion
a transaction holding one channel's advisory lock does not block a create in another channel
two independent Node processes run actual createPlaylist and actual authorization concurrently against the same PostgreSQL at 99 active rows
exactly one process commits a playlist and audit row; the other receives PLAYLIST_LIMIT; final count is 100
existing PG checks continue to verify slot reuse after soft delete, foreign-channel refusal and no lock coupling between channels
